place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 大比 · 半决 · 对马小宝
place.en: Chending Temple · The contest · The semi-final · Against Ma Xiaobao

setup.zh: 半决，在申时。对面是马小宝：一脸丹斑，练气五层，腰里挂着那面白衣人留下的铜镜：「你跪下，叫三声爷爷，我便不照了。」
setup.en: The semi-final, mid-afternoon. Across from you, Ma Xiaobao: face blotched with pill-poison, Qi Refining layer five, at his waist the bronze mirror the man in white left. "Kneel, call me grandfather three times, and I won't shine it."

recap.zh: 半决，你躲一回念一笔公中的账，全外门跟着报数；马小宝的铜镜照向你的胸口，你拿真灵力，用掌心接住了那道光。镜子裂了。一掌三成，他落进了泗水。
recap.en: In the semi-final you read out a line of the common-fund account at every dodge, and the whole outer court counted along; Ma Xiaobao's mirror shone at your chest; you caught the light in your palm with true spirit power. The mirror cracked. One palm at three-tenths, and he landed in the Si.

zh: 申时，半决。对面，马小宝。一面认东西的铜镜。
en: Mid-afternoon, the semi-final. Across from you, Ma Xiaobao. A bronze mirror that recognises things.
"Bark like a dog, and I'll let you lick it once."

story.zh:
小满心里慢慢地算了一笔账。昨天夜里，马小宝拿镜子照铺，没往里灌灵力，镜子上只有火光，木牌都烫成那样；今天灌了灵力，照上胸口，便不是烫一烫的事了。可那镜子是喝马小宝的灵力的：照一回，喝一口；上午照鲁泥鳅，已经喝了三口；一夜吞上去的两层，是虚的，经不起它喝几口。他想：那就让它喝。躲，一回一回地躲，让他一回一回地照，照到只剩最后一口——最后那一口，拿手接。

拿手接，便是拿真灵力去接。一个名册上写着二层的人，拿真灵力去接一面认东西的镜子，接下来是什么，他想不下去了。他只知道，不接，那道光便照进木牌里去。

半决赛在申时。另一个半边，是祁长松对内门那个七层；这一个半边，是他对马小宝。

小满往台上走的时候，阿禾挤过来，塞给他半块烙饼，硬得像一块瓦：「垫垫肚子。空着肚子挨揍，更疼。」他把饼揣进怀里，贴着木牌，贴着那个饼角。

马小宝站在台上，腰里那面铜镜给日头一照，亮得晃眼。他冲台下团团一拱手，扯着嗓子道：「诸位！我这面镜子，是太华山太一宫下来的白衣仙长亲手留给我爹的，能照妖，能退敌，还能照见人心。今天，当着全观，我拿它照一照——」他拿镜子一指小满，「——一个五行杂灵根，输了第一轮，平白冒出十块灵石，躲了师姐三十招，是人，是妖？」台下哄的一声，笑的，嚷的，起哄的，搅成一片。

马小宝又道：「沈小满。你跪下，叫三声爷爷，我便不照了，让你自己走下去。」台下有人起哄：「跪！跪！」一声接一声，起哄的人越来越多，喊到后来，竟有了节拍。便在这一片「跪」声里，人群当中忽然冒出一个嗓子，又尖又哑，破得像一面裂了的锣：「别跪——！」众人回头一看，是孙二狗。他下巴上贴着膏药，站在人堆里，比旁人高出半个头，脸涨得通红。四下里一愣，跟着便哄笑起来：「二狗！你一个输了的，喊什么！」孙二狗的脸红到了耳朵根，可他没有坐下，也没有缩回去，就那么直挺挺地站着。

小满站在台上，看着马小宝。他想起那一年，马小宝站在他家门口，手里捏着桂花糕，说：「学声狗叫，给你舔一口。」他想了想，开口道：「小宝哥。」马小宝道：「嗯？」小满说：「学声狗叫，给你舔一口。」

台下先是一愣，跟着笑声便炸开了。马小宝那张斑斑点点的脸，先是红，再是紫，再是黑。他凑近了一步，声音压得只有台上两个人听得见：「左崖上，你听见了。你在墙里头喘气，我也听见了。」他把镜子从腰里扯了下来。
story.en:
Xiaoman worked out a sum, slowly. Last night Ma Xiaobao had swept the bunks with that mirror without pouring any power into it — nothing on it but firelight, and still the token had burned like that; today, with power poured in, landing on his chest, it wouldn't stop at burning. But the mirror drank Ma Xiaobao's power: one flash, one mouthful; on Lu this morning it had drunk three already; and two layers swallowed in a night were hollow, they couldn't stand many mouthfuls. Then let it drink, he thought. Dodge, and dodge again, and let him flash it again and again, till he's down to the last mouthful — and that last one, take in the hand.

Catch it with his hand meant catch it with true spirit power. A boy written in the register at layer two catching a mirror that recognises things with true spirit power — what came after that, he couldn't think through. He only knew that if he didn't catch it, the light would go into the token.

The semi-finals were at the hour of Shen, mid-afternoon. In the other half, Qi Changsong against the inner-court layer seven; in this half, him against Ma Xiaobao.

As Xiaoman went up to the stage, A He squeezed over and pushed half a flatbread at him, hard as a roof tile: "Line your stomach. A beating on an empty stomach hurts more." He tucked it into his coat, against the token, against that corner of flatbread.

Ma Xiaobao stood on the stage, the bronze mirror at his waist dazzling in the sun. He cupped his fists all round and bawled: "Everyone! This mirror an immortal in white, down from the Taiyi Palace on Mount Taihua, left with my father with his own hands — it shows demons, repels enemies, and shows the heart. Today, before the whole temple, I'll hold it up to —" he pointed it at Xiaoman, "— a mixed-root boy who lost his first round, suddenly turned up with ten stones, and dodged a senior sister for thirty moves. Man, or demon?" The crowd erupted — laughing, shouting, egging on, all in a jumble.

"Shen Xiaoman," said Ma Xiaobao, "kneel, call me grandpa three times, and I won't hold it up; I'll let you walk down yourself." Someone below started up: "Kneel! Kneel!" Again and again, more and more of them, till it took on a beat. And in the middle of the chanting a voice rose from the crowd, shrill and hoarse, cracked like a split gong: "Don't kneel —!" Everyone turned: Sun Ergou, a plaster on his chin, half a head above the crowd, face flushed dark. A pause, then laughter: "Ergou! You lost, what are you yelling for!" Sun Ergou went red to the ears, but he didn't sit down and he didn't shrink back; he just stood there, straight.

Xiaoman stood on the stage and looked at Ma Xiaobao. He remembered that year, Ma Xiaobao at their door with an osmanthus cake: "Bark like a dog and you get a lick." He thought, and said: "Brother Xiaobao." "Hm?" "Bark like a dog," said Xiaoman, "and you get a lick."

For a moment the crowd was stunned, and then the laughter exploded. Ma Xiaobao's blotched face went red, then purple, then black. He stepped closer and dropped his voice so only the two on the stage could hear: "On the left cliff, you heard. You breathing inside that wall — I heard that too." He tore the mirror from his waist.

label.en: Bark like a dog, and you get a lick

exits.means: answers Ma Xiaobao's taunt and fights him for the pill

withdrawn.zh: 马小宝的铜镜又亮了，他笑得更开心了。——再来。
withdrawn.en: Ma Xiaobao's mirror flashes again, and he smiles even wider. — Again.

story.zh:
他两手捧起镜子，脸上的斑「腾」地红了。镜面一亮，一道黄光扑向小满的腿。小满往旁边一跳，那道光打在青石板上，石缝里的草登时白了一片。小满落了地，开口道：「九月初十，公中，一块。」马小宝一愣，又照，他又跳：「十月初一，一块。」又照，他又滚：「冬月初一，两块。因由：畜生也要吃饭。」台下有人「噗」地笑出了声。马小宝咬着牙再照，他再滚：「腊月初一，两块。」

人堆里忽然有人跟着喊了一嗓子，又尖又哑：「九月初十，我也一块！」是孙二狗。跟着便是第二个：「我两块！」第三个：「我也两块——他说我夜里打呼！」外门一百多号人，一个月一个月往那只描金匣子里交的，谁心里没有一本账？方才喊「跪」的那拨人，这时候一个接一个，报的全是数，报到后来，竟也有了节拍。台北面竹椅上，观主拢着手，没有动；周衡站在他身后，翻开了账簿，提起笔，记了一行。马小宝的表伯在台角咳了一声，又咳了一声，咳得谁也没理他。马小宝每照一回，脸上的斑便鼓一回，红一回，捧镜子的手一回比一回抖，喘气一口比一口粗。他站住了，咬着牙道：「躲？你就会躲？」小满没有答。

马小宝咬着牙，把身子里剩下的那一口，全灌进了镜子里。镜面亮得发白，一道黄光，不奔腿，不奔面门，直奔小满的胸口。

那一霎，小满胸口的木牌烫得像一块烧红的铁。这一道，他等了五道。他没有躲。他把一只手抬到了胸前，掌心朝外，把那一线藏了三十几天的火，头一回，扒开了。

那一道黄光撞在他掌心上。它不像打在青石板上那样一扑就散，倒像一根冰锥，往他掌心里钻，钻着找什么东西——找木牌，找木牌里那一缕银。小满五扇门一齐开了，五行那一圈在他身子里转成了一个轮子，转得飞快，全推到那一只手掌上，顶住了它。冷和热在他掌心里撞着，撞得那只手抖成一片。马小宝手里的镜子先是「嗡」的一声，跟着「咔」的一响，镜面上从当中裂开一道缝，裂缝一路爬到镜沿，镜子里的光，灭了。

台下的人没看清。他们只看见马小宝的镜子亮了一亮，便灭了，倒像一盏灯芯受了潮的油灯——灯油，早叫他自己照干了。

马小宝举着那面裂了的铜镜，傻站在台上。他把镜子翻过来看看，又翻过去看看，使劲拍了两下。台下那一片报数，还没歇。小满往前走了一步，又走了一步，已到了马小宝跟前，声音低了下去，低得只有他两个听得见：「那些，是公中的。还有一笔，不在公中——冬月初二夜，左崖，孟有田。」

马小宝的脸白了。

一掌拍出。这一掌，他只出了三成，七成留在手里——三成，打得倒，打不死，旁人看了，只当马小宝自己站不稳。可他算漏了一样：马小宝身子里那点虚灵力，早叫那面镜子喝干了，像一口破缸，外头看着满，底下全是裂缝。三成的力道拍上去，马小宝登时飞了出去，越过了台子，越过了人群，越过了外门的院墙，远远地只听得「扑通」一声，落进了泗水里。

山脚下泗水边，马三那条船还泊着。他把儿子从腊月的泗水里拎了上来。
story.en:
He held it up in both hands, and the blotches on his face flared red. Its face lit, and a beam of yellow light went for Xiaoman's legs. Xiaoman hopped aside; the light struck the bluestone and the grass in the crack went white at once. Xiaoman landed and said: "Tenth of the ninth month, common fund, one stone." Ma Xiaobao faltered, flashed again; he hopped again: "First of the tenth, one." Again, and he rolled: "First of the eleventh, two. Reason: the animal has to eat too." Someone below snorted out a laugh. Ma Xiaobao gritted his teeth and flashed again; he rolled again: "First of the twelfth, two."

Out of the crowd someone suddenly shouted along, shrill and hoarse: "Tenth of the ninth, me too, one!" Sun Ergou. Then a second: "Me, two!" A third: "Me too, two — he said I snore!" A hundred-odd in the outer court, month after month into that gilt box — who didn't carry an account in his head? The same lot who had chanted "kneel" now called out one after another, nothing but numbers, until the numbers too took on a beat. In the bamboo chair north of the stage the abbot sat with his hands in his sleeves and didn't move; behind him Zhou Heng opened his ledger, lifted his brush, and wrote a line. Ma Xiaobao's great-uncle coughed at the corner of the stage, coughed again, and nobody paid him any mind. Every flash, the blotches on Ma Xiaobao's face swelled and flared, the hands holding the mirror shook worse, and each breath came coarser than the last. He stopped and said through his teeth: "Dodge? Is that all you can do?" Xiaoman didn't answer.

Teeth clenched, Ma Xiaobao poured the last mouthful he had into the mirror. Its face blazed white, and a beam of yellow light went not for his legs, not for his face, but straight for Xiaoman's chest.

In that instant the token on Xiaoman's chest burned like red-hot iron. This beam he had waited five beams for. He didn't dodge. He raised one hand before his chest, palm out, and raked open, for the first time, the one thread of fire he had kept hidden for thirty-odd days.

The yellow beam struck his palm. It didn't scatter the way it had on the bluestone; it was like an icicle boring into his palm, boring and searching for something — for the token, for the one wisp of silver inside it. All five of Xiaoman's doors opened at once; the round of the five elements spun in him like a wheel, fast, and he pushed all of it into that one palm and held the light off. Cold and heat crashed together in his palm till his hand shook all over. In Ma Xiaobao's hands the mirror first went *hmmm*, then *crack*: a split opened across the middle of its face and crawled out to the rim, and the light in the mirror went out.

The crowd didn't see it. They only saw Ma Xiaobao's mirror flash and then go out, like an oil lamp with a damp wick — its oil long since burned dry by his own hand.

Ma Xiaobao stood there with the cracked bronze mirror up, dumbfounded. He turned it over and back again and slapped it twice. Below, the counting still hadn't stopped. Xiaoman took a step forward, then another, and stood before Ma Xiaobao, and his voice dropped so low only the two of them could hear: "Those are the common fund's. There's one more, not in the common fund — second night of the eleventh month, the left cliff, Meng Youtian."

Ma Xiaobao's face went white.

One palm. He put out only three-tenths and kept seven in his hand — three-tenths, enough to knock him down and not kill him, so that onlookers would think Ma Xiaobao just lost his footing. But he'd missed one thing in his sums: what hollow power Ma Xiaobao had, the mirror had already drunk dry — a cracked vat, full to look at and split all through underneath. The three-tenths landed and Ma Xiaobao flew — over the stage, over the crowd, over the outer court's wall, and from far off came a single splash, into the Si.

Down at the foot of the mountain, Ma San's boat was still moored. He hauled his son out of the twelfth-month Si.
